m-jacksonville|2024-10-15|38ea27e6|80baf.title:
Chairman Salem convened the meeting and the attendees introduced themselves for the record. The Chair said the committee would discuss the City Council strategic plan in anticipation of starting the process for FY24-25. He noted that the process for developing the strategic plan has changed and evolved over recent years and he doesn’t think it necessarily meets the intent of the legislation creating the strategic plan requirement. The half-percent of the General Fund operating budget that will be allocated to next year’s strategic plan initiatives is $9,416,621 based on the FY24-25 budget. 

Council Member Howland noted that the Ordinance Code requires the development of the plan in the early spring and describes how it relates to the budget, which he said was not followed last year and should be in compliance with the Code. He said he served on the Charter Revision Commission in 2019 and on that body’s Strategic Plan Committee which found it to be a very complicated topic with many Sunshine Law ramifications for who can talk to whom if many community leaders are appointed to a strategic plan governing board. The committee tried to come up with a recommendation that avoided the Sunshine Law restrictions and found it very difficult. He said last year the council allocated some strategic plan funds to a stadium reserve fund and took the other half to divide among several citywide initiatives and more district-specific projects.
